release.body:
An AI-friendly iOS/iPadOS automation service. Tell your agent *"My iPhone is running iCTRL at :8200 — figure out how to drive it."* and it reads the on-device manual and takes it from there. Works with any agent that can make HTTP requests: OpenClaw, Hermes, Minis, Claude Code, Codex and others. ## Downloads ### Which IPA do I need? | File | Needed? | What it is | |---|---|---| | `iCTRLUITests-Runner.ipa` | **Required** | The automation engine. It serves the JSON-RPC API that agents and clients call, and must be running. | | `iCTRL.ipa` | Optional | A companion app for tasks on the phone itself:
• mount the Developer Disk Image without a Mac, and remount it after a reboot
• start and stop the runner
• choose who can reach the runner (this device only / LAN / LAN + nearby)
• see and revoke authorized clients
• read the runner's log live | Skip `iCTRL.ipa` if you mount the Developer Disk Image with Xcode or StikDebug, and manage the runner from its notification or a computer. With a free Apple ID you get three sideloaded apps, and SideStore uses one of them. Install StikDebug *or* the iCTRL app alongside the runner, not both. Both IPAs are unsigned for distribution (ad-hoc, no provisioning profile). Sign them when you install: - **Free Apple ID:** the latest SideStore signs and installs them. Older SideStore releases skip the nested `.xctest`, and the runner then crashes on launch. - **Paid account:** `Scripts/sign-ipa.sh -i iCTRLUITests-Runner.ipa` The runner also needs the Developer Disk Image mounted (Xcode, StikDebug or the iCTRL app). The [README](https://github.com/OpenMinis/iCTRL#installation) covers the whole setup. ## What's new since 1.97.1 ### Nearby discovery: no address to type - **Reach the phone without an address.** Turn on **📡 Nearby Discovery** from the runner's notification or the iCTRL app (it needs Remote Access). Clients can then find the phone: - on the LAN, from any OS; - from a Mac over Apple peer-to-peer Wi-Fi (AWDL), with no shared network at all. The phone only needs Wi-Fi switched on, not joined to anything. - **New client commands:** `python3 ictrl_rpc.py scan` lists discovered phones, and `--nearby ""` replaces `--host`. The first call pairs with the phone (approve once on the phone). - **Strict exposure:** - Nothing is announced on the network unless nearby discovery is on. - The AWDL listener accepts peer-to-peer connections only, and the main listener refuses them. - Nearby discovery can be switched **on** only from the phone itself (notification, iCTRL app or USB). - **Self-healing:** - Advertising follows Wi-Fi off and on, and recovers if the interface is recreated. - A failed listener is rebuilt. - The notification says why nearby discovery isn't ready yet (*turn on Wi-Fi*, *allow Local Network*). ### Who can reach the phone, at a glance - **The status notification's first line** shows one of: 🔒 This device only, 🌐 LAN reachable, or 📡 Nearby discoverable. - **The iCTRL app has a Visibility menu:** 🟢 This device only · safe / 🟡 LAN / 🟡 LAN + nearby. - **LAN addresses are real interfaces only.** VPN or proxy tunnel addresses such as `198.18.0.1` are no longer shown as the phone's address. ### Pairing and keys - **Every pairing is approved on the phone.** The "trusted for 10 minutes" shortcut is gone. - **Limits on requests:** - An unanswered request is refused after 60 s. - Only one request waits at a time, with a 15 s cooldown after a refusal. - Requests from the phone itself have their own slot, so a remote caller can't lock them out. - **Check the key.** The prompt shows a key fingerprint that the client also prints; allow only if they match. - **One key per device.** Clients store keys per device, so a phone paired once works over USB, the LAN and nearby without pairing again. Keys stored under an address by older clients are picked up automatically. - **Local Network permission.** The runner asks for it at launch and reports it. The iCTRL app warns when it's missing; without it, nearby discovery can't work even though LAN clients may still connect. ### iCTRL app - **Authorized Clients:** every key holder, where each last connected from (this device / USB, LAN, nearby, VPN), revoke one or all others. - **Runner Logs:** the runner's log, live, with pause, refresh and filter. - **Visibility menu** (above), and a warning when the runner lacks Local Network access. - **Share a pairing file to iCTRL** from Files, Mail, AirDrop or a chat app when the picker can't reach it. iCTRL confirms when it's stored, or says why it was refused. ### Clients - **Python client:** - Standard library only. LAN pairing no longer needs `pip install cryptography`. - Never sends iCTRL requests through an `http_proxy`. - If macOS Local Network privacy refuses the process, it relays nearby connections through the system `nc`. - **C CLI:** gets the same nearby support when built on macOS. The Linux static binary is rebuilt. ### Server and API - `GET /whoami` and an `X-ICTRL-Device` header on every response identify the device. - `config` adds `nearby_discovery` and `device_name`, and reports nearby status and LAN addresses. Each client's last address and source appear in its session entry. - `config` now validates every parameter before changing any. - A change that restarts the listener replies first instead of returning an empty response. - Read-only polling (`logs`, plain `config`) no longer fills the log. ### Known limitations - Nearby discovery over AWDL needs macOS on the client side. A phone whose screen is off may stop being discoverable over AWDL, as with AirDrop. - With nearby discovery on, iOS also announces the phone's own host name on the LAN, which often contains its owner's name. - Endpoints that need no key (`/schema`, `/skill`, `/remote`, `/whoami`, `/pair`) also answer over AWDL, and the screen stream is not encrypted on any channel. Full details: [#3](https://github.com/OpenMinis/iCTRL/pull/3). ## SHA-256 ``` d28fcb4775885a7161e8c7aa9f247aeb42fe1af1c7fcfc5ce1bbdb1b07b442f2 iCTRLUITests-Runner.ipa 7d9ceaad8eeb486e67d81a688e661f2278113d4ba4f7d3d73cff2f9973881ac7 iCTRL.ipa ```

coverage.semantic_review: bounded semantic scope: 全部compare/每commit patch及文件清单全读，变更机制及相关调用入口（URL通知/RunnerAdmin/Settings stop、whoami/schema、PairingFileStore/DDIMounter、LogBuffer）语义闭合；无关未改历史未全仓审计

assessment.reason: 本轮新增为上游入口鉴权/日志出口/RemotePairing兼容。现有Runner认证与日志原则由SP-204/205覆盖；iCTRL通知/URL scheme与DDI导入不属于Triton当前入口，没有发现可直接纳入的产品缺口。

items.reason: 本地Runner /stop先经过服务持密证明、AES-GCM、session与TTL验证；SP205真实router负例含stop。iCTRL通知确认/深链面本地不存在。
Triton无该锁屏剪贴板通知出口；服务响应日志使用SP204元数据白名单和512字节上限，不复制上游正则脱敏。此结论不代表本项目所有日志出口普查。

items.mechanism: whoami removes device name; schema sync
items.reason: iCTRL客户需容忍name消失；本地无whoami/附近配对key选择器，不能类推删除既有合法本机status字段。
本地无该callback面，且scheme字符串并不构成调用方身份认证；不引入此控制面或视为完全可信。
本地不导入配对文件、不自行挂载DDI；借鉴生产parser与预检一致的原则，不能导入IDevice依赖/签名/DDI能力。

limitations: 未运行上游代码/二进制/设备/签名/DDI；上游修复效果非本地实测。
本次无预算/alias freshness/UI health增量；SP192/SP196/SP200已交付边界继续有效。
固定HEAD server/skill称1.98.13，但GitHub最新非draft Release仍v1.98.12。
DDIMounter primeCryptoProvider仍用lockdown parser，而performMount使用RemotePairing；实际影响未知，不能宣称全挂载兼容已证实。
完整指有界增量及相关机制来源阅读闭合，不代表全仓安全审计；下载全文不是单独的语义证据。
